description: Implement the thin imperative shell over the pure core from FEAT-001: the env snapshot and injected Clock/NonceSource generator traits, the loopback-only bind helper, the shell thiserror error enums, rcgen self-signed TLS generation with printed SHA-256 fingerprint and rustls ServerConfig, the stdin/stdout prompt, the OAuth 1.0a three-leg startup flow (console authorize URL + stdin verifier) signed via sign_leg with a fresh nonce/timestamp per leg, the shared Arc<std::sync::RwLock<AuthPhase>> auth state, the axum router/handlers with verb-first admission, the reqwest Resource-leg upstream forward with a bounded (8 MiB) relay, /internal/status, and main.rs wiring the full startup sequence with anyhow. Depends on FEAT-001 (uses every core function). Leaves the crate building and all FEAT-001 tests still green; cross-FEAT integration tests live in FEAT-003.
steps: shell/env.rs: pub fn snapshot() -> EnvSnapshot reading ONLY ETRADE_CONSUMER_KEY and ETRADE_CONSUMER_SECRET via std::env (the single std::env seam).

shell/clock_nonce.rs: pub trait Clock { fn now_unix(&self) -> Timestamp } and pub trait NonceSource { fn next(&self) -> Nonce } (fresh per call). Real impls: SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).as_secs() with the documented .expect("system clock is before UNIX_EPOCH"); a CSPRNG (rand) producing a fresh Nonce per next(). Provide deterministic test fakes (fixed-time Clock, counter-backed NonceSource) behind #[cfg(test)] or a testutil module for FEAT-003.
shell/server.rs: pub fn bind_addr(ListenPort) -> SocketAddr => SocketAddr::new(IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST), port.0) — the bind address is a code constant, never from data.

shell/error.rs: #[non_exhaustive] thiserror enums with #[from]: TlsError { CertGeneration(#[from] rcgen::Error), RustlsConfig(..) }; OauthFlowError { Http(#[from] reqwest::Error), UnexpectedStatus{endpoint,code}, Parse{endpoint, source: OauthParseError}, Prompt(#[from] std::io::Error), EmptyVerifier }; ProxyError { Upstream(#[from] reqwest::Error)=>502, UpstreamTooLarge{cap}=>502, NotReady=>503 }; ServerError { Bind(#[from] std::io::Error), Tls(#[from] TlsError) }. The OauthFlowError UnexpectedStatus/Parse #[error] messages name the endpoint constant and, on the request-token leg, flag oauth_callback=oob as an unverified assumption to check if that leg 401s.

shell/tls.rs: generate an ephemeral in-memory cert via rcgen 0.14 generate_simple_self_signed(["127.0.0.1".into()]) -> CertifiedKey { cert, signing_key }; compute the fingerprint by passing cert.der() (deref to &[u8]) to core::tls_fingerprint::fingerprint and print it to stdout; build the rustls ServerConfig from signing_key.serialize_der() wrapped as PrivateKeyDer::Pkcs8 and the cert chain from cert.der().clone(). No file is ever written.

shell/prompt.rs: print the authorize URL and the TLS fingerprint to stdout; read the verifier from stdin once, trim surrounding whitespace, and return OauthFlowError::EmptyVerifier if empty after trim (single prompt, no re-prompt). No browser launch.

shell/oauth_flow.rs: pub fn run(&Config, clock: &dyn Clock, nonces: &dyn NonceSource) -> Result<Authorized, OauthFlowError>. Leg 1 (request token): draw a FRESH (nonce, ts) immediately before signing, sign_leg(&SigningInput::RequestToken{consumer_key, callback:"oob"}, consumer_secret, &[], &nonce, &ts), POST to oauth_endpoint_url(REQUEST_TOKEN_PATH) with reqwest, parse the form body with the core parser (also parse-and-log oauth_callback_confirmed at info, non-fatal), non-2xx => UnexpectedStatus{endpoint}. Print the authorize URL from core::authorize_url. Read the verifier via shell::prompt. Leg 2 (access token): draw a FRESH (nonce, ts), sign_leg(&SigningInput::AccessToken{consumer_key, request_token, request_token_secret, verifier}, consumer_secret, &[], &nonce, &ts), POST to oauth_endpoint_url(ACCESS_TOKEN_PATH), parse, build and return Authorized. No value reused across legs.

shell/state.rs: enum AuthPhase { Pending, Ready(Arc<Authorized>) } behind Arc<std::sync::RwLock<AuthPhase>>; the /internal/status phase match reads under a guard that is DROPPED before any serialization/.await (Pending => core::status::status_body_unauthorized(), Ready(a) => status_body_authorized(a)); a poisoned lock at startup is a documented .expect site.

shell/handlers.rs + shell/upstream.rs: an axum fallback handler converts axum's Method and the request path+query into core HttpMethod/&str and calls core::admission::admit. On Forward(upstream_path): if phase is Pending return 503 (ProxyError::NotReady); else clone Arc<Authorized> out and drop the guard, split_query the mapped path into (path, query_params), base_url = upstream_base_url(&path), draw a FRESH (nonce, ts), sign the Resource leg via sign_leg(&SigningInput::Resource{consumer_key, access_token, access_token_secret}, consumer_secret, &query_params, &nonce, &ts), build the wire URL (base_url, or format!("{base_url}?{}", wire_query(&query_params)) when non-empty), GET via reqwest with the signed Authorization header. Relay: buffer the body with a hard cap UPSTREAM_BODY_CAP = 8 MiB (named const; size-limited chunked read; exceeding => ProxyError::UpstreamTooLarge => 502), copy the upstream status, copy only whitelisted headers via core::relay::relay_header_allowed (drop Content-Length and hop-by-hop), send the buffered body; an upstream send/read error => ProxyError::Upstream => 502. On Status: serialize the status body from the current phase. On Reject(MethodNotGet) => 405, Reject(OutOfPrefix) => 404; nothing forwarded upstream on a reject.

shell/server.rs (serve): pub fn/async serve(port: ListenPort, tls, state: Arc<RwLock<AuthPhase>>, clock, nonces) binding bind_addr(port) via axum-server's tls-rustls binder, placing clock/nonces/state in the axum app state so the handler can draw a fresh (nonce, ts) per request. Router: a fallback handler routed through admit (do not pre-route by method/path so the verb-first admission stays the single source of truth).

main.rs: #[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")] async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()>: parse --port (clap derive, default ListenPort(8443)); shell::env::snapshot(); core::config::build_config(&snapshot, port) (on error print a message naming the missing variable and exit non-zero BEFORE binding any socket); shell::tls::generate(); shell::oauth_flow::run(&config, &clock, &nonces) -> Authorized, store Ready(Arc::new(authorized)) in the shared state; shell::server::serve(...). Add .context(..) at config/tls/oauth/bind boundaries; map any error to a non-zero exit. No unwrap/expect outside documented unreachable cases.
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build` succeeds with the shell wired into main (AC-1).
`cargo test` still passes all FEAT-001 core tests plus any shell unit tests added here (AC-3).
bind_addr yields 127.0.0.1 for every port and there is no code path to a non-loopback address (AC-9, unit/property test).
Missing/empty ETRADE_CONSUMER_KEY or ETRADE_CONSUMER_SECRET causes a typed error naming the variable and a non-zero exit with no socket bound (AC-11, exercised at the config layer).
The access token and token secret live ONLY inside the Authorized typestate value in memory; no code path serializes or writes token material to disk (AC-14).
Each OAuth leg and each proxied request draws a fresh (nonce, timestamp) from the injected generators immediately before signing (no reuse); real NonceSource returns distinct nonces across calls.
The upstream relay buffers the body with the 8 MiB cap, copies only whitelisted headers, drops Content-Length/hop-by-hop, and maps upstream/over-cap/not-ready to 502/502/503 respectively.
findings:
COMPLETE and green. cargo build + `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` (zero warnings) + cargo test (101 tests: 79 FEAT-001 core + 22 new shell unit/integration tests) all pass. No live ETrade calls (every shell async test uses a local wiremock server or pure values).

SHELL MODULES IMPLEMENTED (all under src/shell/):
- env.rs: `pub fn snapshot() -> EnvSnapshot` reads ETRADE_CONSUMER_KEY/ETRADE_CONSUMER_SECRET via std::env (the single std::env seam). Consts CONSUMER_KEY_VAR/CONSUMER_SECRET_VAR exported. Unset => None, set-blank => Some("") so the pure validator distinguishes missing vs empty.
- clock_nonce.rs: `pub trait Clock { fn now_unix(&self) -> Timestamp }`, `pub trait NonceSource { fn next(&self) -> Nonce }`. Real impls: `SystemClock` (documented .expect("system clock is before UNIX_EPOCH")), `RandomNonceSource` (rand::thread_rng, 160-bit hex, 40 chars). DETERMINISTIC TEST FAKES ARE PUBLIC (not cfg(test)) so FEAT-003 integration tests in tests/ can use them: `FixedClock::new(secs)` and `CounterNonceSource::new()` (returns "nonce-0","nonce-1",... via AtomicU64, so sequential proxied requests get DISTINCT nonces — this is how to pin the freshness contract).
- error.rs: #[non_exhaustive] thiserror enums with #[from]: `TlsError { CertGeneration(#[from] rcgen::Error), RustlsConfig(#[source] rustls::Error) }`; `OauthFlowError { Http(#[from] reqwest::Error), UnexpectedStatus{endpoint:&'static str, code:u16, callback_hint:&'static str}, Parse{endpoint:&'static str, source: OauthParseError}, Prompt(#[from] std::io::Error), EmptyVerifier }` with consts `OauthFlowError::CALLBACK_HINT` and `NO_HINT`; `ProxyError { Upstream(#[from] reqwest::Error)=>502, UpstreamTooLarge{cap:usize}=>502, NotReady=>503 }`; `ServerError { Bind(#[from] std::io::Error), Tls(#[from] TlsError) }`.
- tls.rs: `pub fn generate() -> Result<Tls, TlsError>` where `pub struct Tls { pub server_config: Arc<rustls::ServerConfig>, pub fingerprint: String }`. Uses rcgen 0.14 generate_simple_self_signed(["127.0.0.1"]) -> CertifiedKey { cert, signing_key }; fingerprint via core::tls_fingerprint::fingerprint(cert.der()); prints it to stdout; builds ServerConfig via `ServerConfig::builder_with_provider(Arc::new(rustls::crypto::aws_lc_rs::default_provider()))` (EXPLICIT provider chosen because reqwest's rustls-tls also pulls in `ring`, so the process-default provider is ambiguous — builder()/install_default would panic/fail; use builder_with_provider). Private key = PrivateKeyDer::Pkcs8(PrivatePkcs8KeyDer::from(signing_key.serialize_der())). No file written.
- prompt.rs: `pub fn prompt_verifier(authorize_url, out: impl Write, input: impl BufRead) -> Result<Verifier, OauthFlowError>` (writer/reader INJECTED, testable) and `pub fn read_verifier(authorize_url) -> Result<Verifier, OauthFlowError>` (wires real stdin/stdout). Single prompt, trims, EmptyVerifier on blank/EOF, no browser launch, no re-prompt.
- state.rs: `pub enum AuthPhase { Pending, Ready(Arc<Authorized>) }`, `pub type SharedState = Arc<std::sync::RwLock<AuthPhase>>`. Helpers: `pending()`, `ready(Authorized)`, `set_ready(&SharedState, Authorized)`, `authorized_handle(&SharedState) -> Option<Arc<Authorized>>` (clones Arc out, drops guard — never held across .await), `status_body(&SharedState) -> StatusBody`. Lock poison = documented .expect. FEAT-003: inject a Pending state with `state::pending()`; inject Ready with `state::ready(authorized)`.
- upstream.rs: `pub const UPSTREAM_BODY_CAP: usize = 8*1024*1024`; `pub struct RelayedResponse { pub status: u16, pub headers: Vec<(String,String)>, pub body: Vec<u8> }`; `pub async fn forward(client: &reqwest::Client, config: &Config, authorized: &Authorized, mapped_path: &str, base_url_override: Option<&str>, clock: &(dyn Clock + Send + Sync), nonces: &(dyn NonceSource + Send + Sync)) -> Result<RelayedResponse, ProxyError>`. Splits query via core::oauth::split_query, draws FRESH (nonce,ts), signs Resource leg via sign_leg, builds wire URL from wire_query(&query_params) (never raw client query), GETs with the signed Authorization header, buffers body with the 8 MiB cap via response.chunk() loop (=> UpstreamTooLarge on overflow), copies only core::relay::relay_header_allowed headers (drops Content-Length + hop-by-hop). NOTE: trait-object params are `&(dyn Clock + Send + Sync)` NOT `&dyn Clock` — REQUIRED so the axum handler future is Send; FEAT-003 must pass `&(dyn ... + Send + Sync)` (an `Arc<dyn Clock + Send + Sync>::as_ref()` works).
- handlers.rs: `pub struct AppState { pub config: Arc<Config>, pub auth: SharedState, pub clock: Arc<dyn Clock + Send + Sync>, pub nonces: Arc<dyn NonceSource + Send + Sync>, pub client: reqwest::Client, pub upstream_base: Option<String> }` (Clone). `pub async fn handle(State(app): State<AppState>, request: Request) -> Response` is the single fallback handler: maps axum Method -> core HttpMethod, extracts uri().path_and_query(), calls admit(). Status => JSON from state::status_body; Forward => 503 if Pending else upstream::forward then relay (status + whitelisted headers + buffered body); Reject(MethodNotGet)=>405, Reject(OutOfPrefix)=>404.
- server.rs: `pub fn bind_addr(ListenPort) -> SocketAddr` = SocketAddr::new(IpAddr::V4(Ipv4Addr::LOCALHOST), port.get()) — loopback is a code constant (AC-9 proptest over all ports). `pub fn router(AppState) -> Router` = Router::new().fallback(handlers::handle).with_state(state) (fallback, NOT any(..) — any() wraps a MethodRouter and does not satisfy the Request-extractor handler; use .fallback directly). `pub fn app_state(config, auth, clock, nonces, upstream_base) -> AppState`. THE SERVE SEAM: `pub async fn serve(port: ListenPort, server_config: Arc<ServerConfig>, config: Arc<Config>, auth: SharedState, clock: Arc<dyn Clock + Send + Sync>, nonces: Arc<dyn NonceSource + Send + Sync>) -> Result<(), ServerError>` — binds via axum_server::bind_rustls(addr, RustlsConfig::from_config(server_config)).serve(app.into_make_service()). FEAT-003 note: `serve` hardcodes upstream_base=None (real host). To drive the proxy handler against a wiremock upstream in an integration test, build the AppState yourself with `server::app_state(config, auth, clock, nonces, Some(mock_uri))` + `server::router(state)` and drive it with axum's testing (e.g. tower::ServiceExt::oneshot, or axum-test), OR add a serve variant that accepts upstream_base if an end-to-end TLS test is wanted. The Pending/503 branch and the counter-nonce freshness assertion are both reachable through app_state/router with a Pending `auth` and a `CounterNonceSource`.
- oauth_flow.rs: `pub async fn run(config: &Config, base_url_override: Option<&str>, clock: &dyn Clock, nonces: &dyn NonceSource, verifier_prompt: impl FnOnce(&str) -> Result<Verifier, OauthFlowError>) -> Result<Authorized, OauthFlowError>`. ADDED PARAMS vs the design sketch: (a) `base_url_override: Option<&str>` so tests point the two legs at a wiremock server (None => oauth_endpoint_url real host); (b) `verifier_prompt` closure so the stdin read is injected (production passes `prompt::read_verifier`). Leg 1 and leg 2 each draw a FRESH (nonce,ts) before signing; leg-1 logs oauth_callback_confirmed (eprintln, non-fatal). Both legs POST with reqwest, parse via core::error::parse_oauth_token_response, map non-2xx => UnexpectedStatus, parse failure => Parse.
- main.rs: `#[tokio::main(flavor="current_thread")] async fn main() -> std::process::ExitCode`. clap derive `Cli { --port: u16 default 8443 }`. Sequence: env::snapshot -> build_config (.context, exits FAILURE before any bind on error) -> tls::generate (.context) -> SystemClock/RandomNonceSource as Arc<dyn ..+Send+Sync> -> oauth_flow::run(&config, None, .., prompt::read_verifier) (.context) -> state::ready(authorized) -> server::serve(..) (.context). main returns anyhow::Result<()> from an inner `run()`; errors printed with `{:#}` and mapped to ExitCode::FAILURE.

DECISIONS / SURPRISES for FEAT-003:
1. axum 0.8 handler MUST take `(State<AppState>, Request)` and be registered via `.fallback(handle)` (NOT `any(handle)`). The handler future must be Send, which forced the upstream::forward trait-object params to be `&(dyn Clock + Send + Sync)` / `&(dyn NonceSource + Send + Sync)`.
2. rustls crypto provider: use `builder_with_provider(Arc::new(rustls::crypto::aws_lc_rs::default_provider()))` explicitly — two providers (aws-lc-rs + ring) are in the dep graph so the default is ambiguous.
3. Test fakes `FixedClock`/`CounterNonceSource` and all state/app_state/router/serve helpers are PUBLIC and reachable from tests/ integration tests; no cargo feature needed.
4. For a wiremock-backed proxy-forward integration test, FEAT-003 should assemble `server::app_state(..., Some(server.uri()))` + `server::router(...)` and drive it in-process (tower oneshot / axum-test), since `serve` itself always targets the real upstream and terminates TLS. The oauth_flow `base_url_override` param already supports pointing the 3-leg flow at wiremock. To assert distinct oauth_nonce across two sequential proxied GETs, inject a `CounterNonceSource` and parse the recorded upstream Authorization headers (wiremock does not validate nonces).
5. No new runtime dependency added beyond the FEAT-001 locked stack; axum kept at default features (no `macros`).
